title: Increasing and decreasing functions

points.text: Increasing/decreasing intervals from the sign of f'(x)

bigPicture: The sign of the derivative tells you whether the graph rises or falls. This turns graph reading into algebra.

keyIdeas.answer: f′(x) > 0 increasing; f′(x) < 0 decreasing; f′(x) = 0 stationary.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you read f′ from the graph of f?
keyIdeas.answer: Where f rises, f′ is above the axis; at turning points f′ crosses zero.

keyTerms.def: range of x where a property holds

misconceptions.right: Decreasing is about f′, not f.
State interval with correct inequality signs.

practice.prompt: Find the interval on which f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 12x + 1 is increasing.
Using the GDC, sketch y = f′(x) for f(x) = x⁴ − 4x² and state where f is decreasing.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: How does a sign change in f′ classify a stationary point?
